  • Puzzle 4: One frame, from tree to pixels

    Compose makes a frame in three phases, always in this order. Composition runs what's marked and updates the tree of nodes. Layout passes constraints down, measures each child once within them, lets each parent pick its own size, then places each child relative to its parent. Drawing has each node paint itself onto a canvas. Each phase can be skipped when its inputs didn't change.

The problem

Puzzles 6 and 7 stayed inside the shared screen. Puzzle 5 said the part of Compose that meets the phone is written per platform, and on iOS the whole screen is drawn inside one UIKit view controller (the KMP course, puzzle 15). Now the edges. Our shared bookmarks screen already runs on Android. On iOS it sits under the app’s existing navigation bar. The search field uses UIKit because it needs a behavior specific to Apple’s text field. Which object hosts which?

See it

Save this diagram as a GIF

The building block

A hosting boundary is where one UI system gives a region to the other. There are two different directions in this example.

NeedWhat to useOwner of the surrounding region
Show the shared bookmarks in an existing iOS appComposeUIViewControllerUIKit or a SwiftUI wrapper around that controller
Put a native search field inside the shared screenUIKitViewCompose

A view controller manages an area of UIKit UI. The controller returned by ComposeUIViewController hosts the shared composables. The rendering phases still run inside that shared region. SwiftUI can show that controller using UIViewControllerRepresentable, an adapter that lets SwiftUI display a UIKit controller.

Within the shared area, UIKitView can host a UITextField, Apple's text input view. Its factory creates the view. Its update callback can copy the latest shared value onto that existing view when the displayed text differs. User edits go in the other direction, through a native callback that updates the shared value.

For a field driven by shared state, make both directions explicit: user edit → shared value → displayed text. If you change the shared value through another action, such as Clear, the native field needs the update path to show the change.

Go deeperA reset while the keyboard is open
The field writes edits to shared state, but a tap on Clear changes only that state. Which missing edge can leave old text on screen?

The native edit callback handles the other direction. The update callback has to copy the cleared shared value into the existing native field.

Back to the main puzzle

The analogy

Our company's play is a guest in another theatre: the theatre's own stage manager (UIKit) decides where it plays and when. Inside our play, one scene uses a real piece of the host theatre's machinery, a working lift (the native field). We built the set around it, but the lift has its own controls: we tell it where to go (update), and it tells us when someone rode it (the edit callback).

What you now know

A shared screen can sit inside an iOS view controller. Inside that screen, a native view can be embedded with distinct creation and update steps.
